2608.20202.title: MemTrapBench: Benchmarking Cognitive Traps in LLM Memory Use
2608.20202.paper_summary: Memory has become a key component of large language models, enabling them to retain information and learn from long-term interactions. However, existing memory benchmarks mainly evaluate whether information is correctly extracted, stored, and retrieved, while largely overlooking how retrieved memories reshape model reasoning and affect performance on the current task. We identify memory-induced cognitive traps: even faithfully recorded and semantically relevant memories can distort model reasoning or beliefs and degrade current task performance. To systematically evaluate these failure modes, we introduce MemTrapBench, which covers two forms of cognitive traps: Reasoning Fixation and Belief Distortion. Experiments across two model families and five representative memory frameworks show that MemTrapBench is challenging: all evaluated memory strategies underperform the no-memory setting, with even the strongest methods suffering drops of more than 10%. To mitigate these cognitive traps, we propose AdaptiveMem, a simple yet effective inference-time method that instructs LLMs to avoid memory traps. AdaptiveMem mitigates cognitive traps on MemTrapBench while preserving or improving performance on standard memory benchmarks across diverse memory frameworks.
2608.20202.paper_summary_zh: 記憶已成為大型語言模型的關鍵組成部分，使它們能夠保留資訊並從長期互動中學習。<lb/>然而，現有的記憶基準主要評估資訊是否正確提取、儲存和檢索，卻在很大程度上忽視了檢索到的記憶如何重塑模型推理並影響當前任務的表現。<lb/>我們識別出記憶引發的認知陷阱：即使是忠實記錄且語義相關的記憶也可能扭曲模型推理或信念，並降低當前任務的表現。<lb/>為了系統性地評估這些失敗模式，我們引入了MemTrapBench，涵蓋兩種形式的認知陷阱：推理固著和信念扭曲。<lb/>在兩個模型家族和五個代表性記憶框架下的實驗顯示，MemTrapBench具有挑戰性：所有評估的記憶策略在無記憶設定下的表現均不佳，即使是最強的方法也遭遇超過10%的下降。<lb/>為了減輕這些認知陷阱，我們提出了AdaptiveMem，一種簡單而有效的推理時方法，指導大型語言模型避免記憶陷阱。<lb/>AdaptiveMem在MemTrapBench上減輕了認知陷阱，同時在多樣的記憶框架下保持或提高了標準記憶基準的表現。
